articles.title: 65 Years Later, the Best "Peanuts' Linus Quote Is Still an All-Time Great Comic Strip Moment
articles.summary: This got a little watered down as the strip continued, and Linus isn’t quite as intellectual in the various cartoon adaptations (his Bible monologue in A Charlie Brown Christmas notwithstanding), but he has a theologian's knowledge of the Bible and can pontificate like a Ph.D. in philosophy.
body: You can generally map most of the main characters in Charles Schulz's Peanuts onto a sort of body/brain model. Snoopy is the strip's imagination. Charlie Brown is its undiagnosed anxiety. Lucy Van Pelt is a stand-in for the specific rage of being a little kid in a world that was made for adults. If you accept that premise, then Linus Van Pelt is the brains of the operation.

Peanuts ran for just under 50 years. While Linus wasn't part of the core cast until 1952 (two years into the strip's existence) and didn't start talking until 1954, he quickly became one of the central characters. As a result, if you're looking to put together a top 10 or 15 or 20 list of Linus's best lines, you're somewhat spoiled for choice. It'd almost be easier to group them by topic, like how a few Peanuts collections are arranged by specific themes.

If you had to simply pick one, though, my choice is from relatively early in Peanuts' run, on April 26, 1961. It's not quite a political cartoon, but it's one of the few examples of Peanuts getting close enough to one to count.

articles.title: 5 Nintendo Games You Need to Play at Least Once
articles.summary: Nintendo 's reputation for decades of certified bangers is well-earned, though between new releases and the classics that hog all the attention, it's easy to overlook some of the company's more influential games.
body: I'm not gonna tell you to go play Super Mario Bros. 3 or A Link to the Past. You should play them, but you've probably heard that from a dozen other people already. This list is more interested in examining a few pivotal games from Nintendo's history that marked turning points for the company, either for the risk involved in making them or by representing a high point in creative design that informed Nintendo's future strategies. All of these are available in some form or another on modern hardware, either via remakes, Nintendo Switch Online 's retro library, or even on PC thanks to later ports.

Nintendo played it safe with the GameCube. You might think otherwise, what with Mario Sunshine sending the plumber on a goop-cleaning vacation and The Wind Waker turning Link and Zelda into cartoons. These were still Mario and Zelda games, though. And what is Luigi's Mansion, but a Mario is Missing that doesn't suck? Pikmin was something new and wildly different than anything Nintendo had developed for years: A real-time strategy game (a genre that, nearly three decades later, remains quite niche) starring a corporate lackey and an army of sentient, expendable vegetables.

articles.title: Netflix Reveals New Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 Trailer and Images at Anime NYC
articles.summary: A new trailer and images from Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 have been revealed by Netflix, giving us a closer look at the high-octane action and heartbreaking tragedy we can expect from this latest foray into Night City.
body: An English-language trailer for the critically-acclaimed anime’s second season has hit the internet to kick off Anime NYC. We finally get to hear Clancy Brown ( Detroit: Become Human, Avatar the Last Airbender ) as Weak Kingsley, a veteran Edgerunner who we see fall into the throes of cyberpsychosis and blast some chooms with his pistol. You know, typical Cyberpunk stuff.

We also get a glimpse of him taking an assignment from a concerned mother in a diner, who mentions her daughter, as well as a shot of him sitting by Talia Yang as she lies in a hospital bed. “Losing yourself… that’s worse than death,” Kingsley says in a voiceover.

D, a Snake Nation nomad, also gets some time to shine; we see him slotting a datashard into his neck as a voiceover says: “Those burns… I didn’t know anyone else survived. You’ve been out for blood? All this time?”

A burning campsite flashes across the screen, along with clips of the usual Night City ultraviolence. We see a shot of Talia in the rain, then D and Roman Carax standing by a burning corpse at night in the desert. Something crazy is happening with D’s hair here as Roman says in a voiceover: “You’re a weapon? A weapon made out of people?”

articles.title: 5 Classic Anime That Will Never Need Remakes
articles.summary: That said, some classic anime should never be remade. One-of-a-kind entries like Paranoia Agent (2004) and Revolutionary Girl Utena (1997) feel timeless, and the unique circumstances that helped shape these shows can never be replicated.
body: In the age of remakes and reboots, it makes sense for most classic anime to get a do-over. Think Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood (2009), Hunter x Hunter (2011), or Hellsing Ultimate (2006) — these remakes are now considered definitive as they hew closer to the source material. Of course, a newer adaptation doesn’t render older ones obsolete, especially in the case of acclaimed classics like Naruto or Dragon Ball, which will forever be adored in spite of their flaws.
Although most stories benefit from a fresh take or a new style of animation, here are five classic anime that should never, ever get remakes.

articles.title: There Will Never Be Another Game Like Metal Gear Solid 4
articles.summary: “Nowadays, anyone with a computer can get combat training,” Big Mama says. “The FPS games these children love are distributed for free by these companies. Of course, it’s all just virtual training. It’s so easy for them to get absorbed by these war games.
body: Midway through Metal Gear Solid 4: Guns of the Patriots, just as Solid Snake is about to ride into a high-octane motorcycle shootout, director Hideo Kojima forces players to have a come-to-Jesus moment. Big Mama stops to explain that her troops are child soldiers. They’re largely orphans who grew up surrounded by warfare. They started working in the arms industry, and moved to combat as a way to support their younger siblings while getting revenge on the companies responsible for killing their parents. The dystopian monologue is capped off by a sobering reality check.

articles.title: Netflix Confirms Blue Eye Samurai Will End With Third and Final Season
articles.summary: Netflix has revealed that Blue Eye Samurai will officially end with a third and final season. Netflix showed off a host of upcoming content at Anime NYC today, including a new trailer and images for Blue Eye Samurai Season 2.
body: Netflix told us that Season 3 will serve as the final conclusion for the series, tying up Mizu’s dramatic journey for good.
Blue Eye Samurai Season 2 was first confirmed in December 2023, with co-creators Amber Noizumi and Michael Green releasing a joint statement excitedly revealing the news.

"When we started this project, we made a commitment to take this very personal story set in Edo-period Japan and bring it to life in the most authentic and beautiful way possible. Our animators, historians, musicians, martial artists and voice cast made this a reality beyond our expectations," they said.

"We are thankful to our entire team and to our viewers from all over the world who have shown such passion for Mizu and her path of revenge. Mizu has a lot more blood to spill! We are deeply grateful to our incredible partners at Netflix for letting the journey continue."

articles.title: Double Your PlayStation 5 Storage With This 1TB PCIe M.2 SSD for Just $136.39 Shipped
articles.summary: Newegg is offering the best price I've seen this year for a high-speed PS5-compatible SSD. Newegg via its official AliExpress storefront is offering a KingSpec XG7000 1TB PCIe 4.0 M.2 NVMe Solid State Drive for an impressively low price of $136.39 with free shipping (you'll need to be signed in to…
body: Installing an SSD in your PlayStation 5 console is super easy and won't void your warranty. It's also a near essential upgrade. With games taking up as much as 100GB of space apiece, it's very easy to max out the PS5's stock 1TB storage, and it's not unheard of to max out an additional 2TB of space.

The KingSpec XG7000 is very fast for a "budget" M.2 SSD. This is a PCI-E 4x4 drive with transfer speeds of up to 7,400MB/s read and 6,600MB/s write, which passes Sony's recommended minimum requirement of 5,5000MB/s. Despite the fact that this is a budget SSD, the XG7000 is equipped with TCL 3D NAND flash memory. Most cheap SSDs use QLC memory, which has slower sustained speeds and a shorter lifespan. To save costs, the XG7000 doesn't have onboard DRAM, and instead uses HMB, or onboard system memory for buffering. For PS5 gamers, there's no difference.

Although you can get by without a heatsink, Sony officially recommends one, as noted in their FAQ section in their install guide. The KingSpec XG7000 doesn't include one out of the box. Fortunately, you can find one on Amazon for about $6 and they're very simple to install (most are attached with adhesive).

articles.title: Step Aside, GTA 6 Leaks, We Have To Talk About Zork
articles.summary: Ongoing GTA 6 leaks might be the biggest gaming news story happening right now, but there's something much more important to discuss: Zork. We finally know what From Software's new Switch 2 exclusive, The Duskbloods, actually is, and among the many details we've gotten is a reveal of some of the…
body: That's Zork on the right, a man in an exceedingly pear-like diving suit who wields a hunk of undersea cable as a weapon. He can also howl, fire a cannon carried on his back, and launch his entire body at enemies, which can actually knock enemy players off the map in the ultimate form of humiliation.

In speaking with From Software's Hidetaka Miyazaki recently, our own Jake Dekker had to ask about Zork. "There’s always going to be your traditional characters, especially in a vampire-like game," Miyazaki said. "You have your traditional Victorian Gothic characters, and then you have other characters that are a little bit more off to the side with Asian influences [like Trang Lanh]. I think Zork is basically as far off to the side as you can get, where he’s a bit of a wild card. It’s always fun to have characters like that, and there’s always people who like characters like that."

articles.title: OK, Vice City does look pretty damn impressive from the air
articles.summary: We've pulled lots of interesting little details out of the purported Grand Theft Auto 6 gameplay clips being posted by " Cyberleek " this week. In the first couple we saw a possible morality system and stamina meter, and in the next two we got a better look at combat and spied some other Red Dead…
body: My takeaway was that Grand Theft Auto 6 won't necessarily be a revolutionary new kind of game, but will be impressive for the same reason Rockstar games typically are: The absurd amount of effort and money the studio puts into making them as big and detailed as the mainstream hardware of the day can manage.

After seeing the latest leaked clip, which shows a biplane surveying the fictional state of Leonida and cruising over Vice City, my perspective hasn't really changed, but I'm definitely a lot more wowed than I was after seeing a bit of typical GTA carjacking.

The city, which is only a portion of GTA 6's full map, looks enormous from the air, and densely packed with detail. Across a couple minutes of video, we see what looks like a military base, small farms, dozens of mid- and high-rise apartments and office buildings, an arena, a construction site, grimier looking commercial districts, a huge marina and waterways running through the city, bridges, and tangled freeway interchanges. Phew.
Similar reactions are being shared in the Gaming Leaks and Rumors subreddit: "Yea this is the first clip out of all of these leaks that actually made me go 'holy shit,'" said one commenter.

The bullet marks spell out "LEEK," seemingly proving that CyberLeek has access to a playable build of GTA 6. Before that footage, the video features a blue-and-yellow prop plane flying over what appears to be Vice City. At one point, the game pauses while the player swaps through different radio stations, like V-Rock playing "For What It's Worth" by Stevie Nicks and Back Country Radio playing "Rhinestone Cowboy" by Glen Campbell. There's even Symphony FM.

GTA 6 is set to get an official "Extended Look" trailer exactly a week from today on August 27. That footage will first appear on Netflix on 3 PM ET, before then becoming available on Rockstar's YouTube channel at 9 PM ET. GTA 6 is set to come out November 19 on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S.

articles.title: Metal Gear Solid 4: Guns of the Patriots review
articles.summary: The new best way to play Kojima's strangest sequel.
body: It's no longer about avoidance, visibility, or tension. It's an endless series of "stealth action" games trivializing the uncertainty of sneaking and pushing players into open conflict. The age of camouflage has become the age of tall grass: stealth is no longer treated as a genre worthy of big budgets, but an optional feature of conventional action games. [Takes a long drag from a cigarette] Stealth has changed. And when the player's visibility is under total control… espionage becomes routine.

Metal Gear Solid 4: Guns of the Patriots was at the vanguard of the stealth action shift in 2008—but playing it today, the particular way it mixes mercurial stealth and heavy weaponry is anything but routine. Snake is outfitted with a tranq pistol, non-lethal CQC training, and the latest OctoCamo sneaking suit, an ingenious invention of espionage that automatically camouflages the user to their surroundings. In his other pocket are enough guns to arm a strike force—SMGs, shotguns, ARs, RPGs, a rail gun—customizable with Create-a-Class attachments.

articles.title: Miyazaki suggests FromSoftware is keen to return to single-player games after The Duskbloods and Elden Ring: Nightreign
articles.summary: Hidetaka Miyazaki, the president of FromSoftware and director of so many revered Soulsian games, has suggested the studio is keen to return to making single-player games after The Duskbloods.
body: Speaking to IGN, Miyazaki explained it was a coincidence that 2025's Elden Ring: Nightreign and The Duskbloods were both multiplayer games. "It's funny because there was never really any big plan that these two games [Nightreign and The Duskbloods] would both release next to each other," he said.

"I mean, that's a different director," he added, referring to Junya Ishizaki who helmed Nightreign, "but both of those ideas just coincided with being multiplayer games. It's not necessarily some big reveal saying that this is the direction we plan to go moving forward. We still have a heavy focus on single-player content as well. This is just something that happened to work out the way it did."

It was while continuing this thought, and saying it had been fun to make a multiplayer game, that Miyazaki said: "But it's like, the more you work on something multiplayer for a long time, if anything, it scratches that itch only to want to make something single-player again."
points: Hidetaka Miyazaki, the president of FromSoftware and director of so many revered Soulsian games, has suggested the studio is keen to return to making single-player games after The Duskbloods.
